tier_reason: C stands: competitor's wiki page; not faster on equal footing.

corrections.tradeoffs: In-memory (malloc) or file-backed HTTP reverse-proxy cache configured through the VCL language, which gives fine control over caching and request handling but has a learning curve; no TLS termination in the core (needs Hitch or similar); multi-threaded, so a hit costs more cores than one nginx worker.
corrections.maintenance_status: unknown (GitHub repository archived 2026-02-16; development moved to Vinyl Cache at code.vinyl-cache.org, whose 9.0.0 release in April 2026 is known only from a search snippet; the site did not resolve)
corrections.caveats: Enricher: harness defects in the nuster wiki: the 512 B and 1 KB rows over 1 Gbps run near link saturation (nginx 12 workers at about 0.89-0.93 Gbit/s of HTTP payload, derived from page data), so they measure the link; the loopback runs put wrk -t 100 on the same 12 cores as the server; Varnish threads stayed at defaults while nginx was tuned. Correction: the 30-40 ms miss delay in issue #1923 came from a Node.js backend that sent no Content-Length, not from Varnish, so it is not a Varnish tradeoff.

tier_reason: C stands: vendor-run, snippet only, no harness.

corrections.hardware: AWS i3.4xlarge (3-node clusters, 48 vCPUs in total) and i3.metal (4 ScyllaDB nodes, 288 vCPUs) against 40 x i3.4xlarge for Cassandra (640 vCPUs, about 2.22x the ScyllaDB vCPUs, derived from page data); the vendor's '2.5x' refers to hardware cost, not vCPUs. ScyllaDB ran CentOS 7.9 and Cassandra Ubuntu 20.04, single availability zone, per search-result text.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: in the '4 vs 40' test Cassandra had 640 vCPUs against ScyllaDB's 288 (2.22x, derived), not 2.5x (that is the vendor's cost ratio); the two sides ran different OSes (CentOS 7.9 against Ubuntu 20.04) in one availability zone. Only lead for independent evidence: a 2025 Applied Computer Systems YCSB study, abstract only (reference-global.com and doaj.org unreachable). Open issues report P99 spikes during topology changes, tablet split, repair and compaction (#20895, #23441, #24025, #3615). Category: a distributed wide-column OLTP store filed under columnar-analytics for lack of an OLTP category.

tier_reason: C stands: vendor numbers uncorroborated; the independent benchmark shows it slower.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: MaibornWolff harness flaws: single unreplicated PostgreSQL against a 3-node replicated YugabyteDB; databases tested at different times on whatever version was newest (cross-run); the temperature-stats query was rewritten from avg() to sum()/count() for YugabyteDB only; the newest-per-device query failed. YSQL queries ran 3x-14x slower (derived from page data). Tracking issue #15858 reports colocated aggregates up to 16x and DISTINCT up to 130x slower than PostgreSQL. The vendor's per-workload numbers against Cassandra remain uncorroborated (D defensible if corroboration is required). Category: distributed OLTP filed under columnar-analytics for lack of an OLTP category.
